s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative corneal inflammation with deep stromal involvement
salient_findings: Brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma
Central infiltrate involving all corneal layers on optical coherence tomography
Decreased visual acuity in the right eye
key_facts: Patient underwent DSAEK in the right eye
History of eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa 9 months before DSAEK
Postoperative course was initially uneventful under topical and systemic corticosteroids
Keratitis developed in the right eye 2 months after DSAEK
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/200 in the right eye
Pupils were isocoric and isoreactive without an afferent pupillary defect
No pain with ocular movements
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showed brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma
Anterior chamber was deep and clear
Intraocular pressure and fundus examination were normal

shortlist.label: Fungal keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma are consistent with fungal infection

shortlist.label: Acanthamoeba keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of eye infection and deep stromal involvement are risk factors for Acanthamoeba keratitis

shortlist.label: Bacterial keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Postoperative corneal inflammation with deep stromal involvement could be caused by bacterial infection

shortlist.label: Nocardia keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Nocardia is a rare but possible cause of postoperative keratitis, especially with deep stromal involvement

shortlist.label: Mycobacterial keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Mycobacterial infection is a rare but possible cause of keratitis, especially in the context of deep stromal involvement and postoperative inflammation

raw.rationale: The presence of brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma, as seen on slit-lamp biomicroscopy, is consistent with fungal keratitis, which often presents with distinctive infiltrates and can occur after ocular surgery or trauma, especially in the context of previous eye infection and corticosteroid use.

rejected.label: Acanthamoeba keratitis
rejected.why: Typically associated with contact lens use and more pronounced pain, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Bacterial keratitis
rejected.why: Usually presents with more acute onset, significant conjunctival hyperemia, and discharge, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Nocardia keratitis
rejected.why: Less common and often associated with soil or water exposure, which is not indicated in the patient's history.

rejected.label: Mycobacterial keratitis
rejected.why: Rare and typically associated with specific risk factors such as trauma with soil exposure or use of contaminated water, not mentioned in the vignette.
